title: E0023: Instability, Abstractness, and Distance from Main Sequence
plain_english: Reports namespace-level coupling metrics when they exceed configured thresholds: Instability (I), Abstractness (A), and Distance from Main Sequence (D).
why_matters: These metrics help evaluate whether a namespace has a healthy balance between stability and abstraction. - **Stable, abstract namespaces** (for example, shared interfaces) are easier to depend on safely. - **Unstable, concrete namespaces** (for example, implementation details) are easier to change when few other parts depend on them. - Namespaces far from this balance can be hard to change or provide little practical value.
bad_example:
<?php
namespace App\Service;

class PaymentService
{
    public function __construct(
        private \App\Repository\OrderRepository $orders,
        private \App\Repository\UserRepository $users,
        private \App\Gateway\StripeGateway $stripe,
    ) {}
}
good_example:
<?php
namespace App\Service;

interface PaymentGateway
{
    public function charge(int $amount): void;
}

class PaymentService
{
    public function __construct(private PaymentGateway $gateway) {}
}
what_it_checks: `Ce` (efferent coupling): number of external types this namespace depends on.
`Ca` (afferent coupling): number of classes outside this namespace that depend on classes in this namespace.
Higher `I` means the namespace depends on many others relative to how many depend on it.
`abstract`: number of abstract classes and interfaces in the namespace.
`total`: total number of classes in the namespace.
Lower values are closer to the ideal balance.
`E0023:distance` when `D > max_distance` and both instability and abstractness are computable.
